statement.p: (a) Find the point Q that is a distance 0.1 from the point P = (2, 5) in the direction of \mathbf{v} = \left\lt -2,-1\right>. Give five decimal places in your answer.
(b) Use P and Q to approximate the directional derivative of f(x,y) = \sqrt{x+3y} at P, in the direction of \mathbf{v}.
(c) Give the exact value for the directional derivative you estimated in part (b).

static.solution:
(a) The unit vector \mathbf{u} in the same direction as \mathbf{v} is \mathbf{u} = \frac{1}{\Vert \mathbf{v}\Vert} \mathbf{v} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \mathbf{v} = \langle \frac{-2}{\sqrt{5}}, \frac{-1}{\sqrt{5}} \rangle \approx \left\lt -0.894427,-0.447214\right>.
The vector \mathbf{w} of length 0.1 in the direction of \mathbf{v} is \vec w = 0.1\vec u = \left\lt -0.0894427,-0.0447214\right> The displacement vector from P to Q is \mathbf{w}. Hence Q = (2,5) + (-0.0894427, -0.0447214) = (1.91056, 4.95528).
(b) Since the distance from P to Q is 0.1, the directional derivative of f at P in the direction of Q is approximately f_{u} \approx \frac{f(Q)-f(P)}{0.1} = \frac{4.0959 - 4.12311}{0.1} = -0.2721.
(c) We have f_x = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+3y}}\quad\mbox{and}\quad f_y = \frac{3}{2\sqrt{x+3y}}, so \nabla f(2,5) = \left\lt 0.121268,0.363803\right>.
The directional derivative at P=(2, 5) in the direction of \mathbf{u} is f_u(2,5) = \nabla f(2,5)\cdot \mathbf{u} = -0.271163.
